author: IGN
description:
Get a look at the Announcement Trailer for Steam to Electric, a voxel-based rail tycoon developed by Galaxy Grove. Players will assemble a streamlined and efficient railway network to transport passengers, unlock historical train inventions, and make the grand transition from steam to electric. Steam to Electric is coming soon to PC (Steam).

author: IGN
description:
Take a look at gameplay and more from Luckrot in this launch trailer for the roguelike shooter set in a dystopian, livestreamed gameshow. Obliterate waves of deformed freaks, earn donations from your sadistic audience and gamble your earnings for upgrades. Your life is a Performance. Your Death is Content. Luckrot is out now on Steam.

#ign #gaming
title: Luckrot - Official Launch Trailer

author: IGN
description:
Take a look at the announcement trailer for Beware of the Cartographer!, an upcoming point & click puzzle adventure game where you map a mysterious land during the Age of Enlightenment. Draw the border between two warring kingdoms. Meet the locals. Juggle their demands with the requirements of your mission. Ethical dilemmas, secret plots, strange phenomena… will you be able to bring peace back to the land? Beware of the Cartographer! will be available on Steam (Windows & MacOS) in 2027. A demo is out now on Steam.

#ign #gaming
title: Beware of the Cartographer! - Official Announcement Trailer

author: IGN
description:
Take a look at the Reverse Collapse announcement trailer for Sunborn’s upcoming third-person shooter global flagship title.

Set in a near-future world shaped by Collapse particle pollution and global conflict, Players battle across a fractured universe shaped by multiple competing races.

Developed in Unreal Engine 5, Reverse Collapse will be available on both PC & Mobile and offer cross-platform gameplay and progression.

Presented by Sunborn Games
title: Reverse Collapse - Official Announcement Trailer

author: IGN
description:
For a long time, Mortal Kombat’s 1995 live-action movie set the bar as far as video game-to-movie adaptations go. Not a high bar to clear, to be sure, but the bottom line is the 1995 video game adaptation understood what fans wanted: great martial arts, plenty of cheese, a respect for the source material, and a lot of Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa mean-mugging the camera and saying “Your soul is mine!”
Now, with Mortal Kombat II about to hit theaters, we are asking the question: Does the 1995 Mortal Kombat stand the test of time? Watch our Flashback Review to find out the answer!
title: Review: Mortal Kombat (1995) Is a Bad Movie, But Does Anybody Care?

description: Don't miss the 'A Paranaturally Warped Manhattan' Overview for Control Resonant, an upcoming action-adventure sequel developed by Remedy Entertainment.
